answers.answer: For each office card, roll one die simultaneously; add one for each fatigue on that card, and the Chairman also adds one. A modified 1–2 has no effect, 3–4 adds fatigue, and 5+ retires the member. Move the retiring member to Pensioners, flip the office card to Vacant Offices, and return that card's fatigue to supply.
answers.evidence: London Season: ‘Modified 1–2: nothing; 3–4: add fatigue; 5+: retire. Move retiree to Pensioners, flip card into Vacant Offices, return its fatigue to supply.’

answers.answer: Only players who retired at least one pensioner select or discard a display card. They act in descending order of actual total retirement spending. Ties go to the player with most total windows, including new prizes, then clockwise from the PM; an acting player may peek at display blackmails. Do not replace cards during selection. If the display empties, skip every remaining eligible player. After selection, discard every card left and refill exactly three cards (prestige faceup, blackmail facedown), even if nobody selected a card. Return all unused Pensioners to their supplies.
answers.evidence: London Season: ‘Players who retired at least one pensioner’; order is ‘descending actual total retirement spending’; ties use ‘most total windows’ then ‘clockwise from PM’; ‘discarding all remaining cards and refilling exactly three’; return remaining Pensioners to supplies.

answers.answer: A player takes one chosen family action and places their opportunity marker on it. If that marker was already on the chosen action at the start of the phase, that action may be taken twice. Only the latest passed extra-action law can be used; its extra action is not doubled by the marker and does not move the marker. With four vacant offices and the marker already on Enlist Writer, the doubled action can enlist two writers, and the vacancy bonus adds one writer once that turn, for three total.
answers.evidence: Family: ‘If your marker was already on that action at phase start, you may take that action twice’; extra-action law ‘receives no opportunity-marker doubling’; Enlist Writer: ‘place one additional writer once this turn, so a doubled Writer action can place three total.’

answers.answer: After family actions, while Debt and applicants both remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and reduce Debt by one; repeat until either Debt or applicants run out. If there is no Debt, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible while preserving their order. Seek Share money is paid to the bank, not to Company treasuries.
answers.evidence: Family: ‘move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one’; with no Debt, ‘slide remaining applicants as far right as possible, preserving order’; seeking ‘never pays family cash into Company treasuries.’

answers.answer: Fill vacant offices in ascending order by the number on their card backs. For an ordinary own-family hire, every other player represented in that office's candidate pool must give verbal consent; Chairman elections and Commander appointments are exempt. On promotion, transfer the old officeholder's fatigue to the new card and insert the old card, vacant, in ascending hiring order. If there is no candidate or the designated hirer is vacant, skip that office; it remains vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.
answers.evidence: Hiring: ‘Fill vacant offices in ascending number’; own-family hiring requires consent of ‘every other player represented in that office's candidate pool’; promotion transfers fatigue; absent candidate or hirer means skip and office takes no actions.

answers.answer: The former Chairman first announces the number of shares needed for a pure majority, meaning more than half of current shares. Shareholders may campaign; the first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins. If nobody gets the required support, the former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including themself. If the Court is empty, the former Chairman automatically returns, subject to having a family member available or able to take one from a prize. The elected Chairman's piece remains a Company share for dividends, majority and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in firms.
answers.evidence: Chairman election: ‘pure majority (more than half of current shares)’; if no candidate gets support, ‘former Chairman picks any shareholder including self’; elected share ‘still counts as a share’ but ‘cannot be traded or invested in firms.’

answers.answer: Before a Company-office check, commit resources and cash; all cash comes from the acting office's treasury and is paid to the bank. Gather dice, subtract penalties, and roll. Use the lowest die: 1–2 succeeds; 3–4 fails and can be retried if resources and office-specific limits allow; 5–6 is catastrophic, ends that office's actions, returns its officeholder to supply, discards fatigue, and flips its card into Vacant Offices. Do not take an action that has no effect or chance of success, such as trading with no ship or deploying without dice merely to trigger officer losses. Specific Commander and firm procedures can modify the general check.
answers.evidence: Success checks: cash is from ‘that acting office's treasury and is paid to the bank’; lowest die 1–2 success, 3–4 retryable failure, 5–6 catastrophe with officeholder, fatigue and card destinations; dead actions are prohibited.

answers.answer: The Chairman may add up to three Debt without consent, receiving £5 Balance per Debt. Each further advance requires consent from players controlling a majority of Company shares (the Chairman counts), and Debt can never pass the end of its track. The Chairman must allocate all Balance to other offices' treasuries, reducing Balance by the amount transferred. Borrowing and allocation may be interleaved while observing the borrowing limits; money already in an office stays there for that office to use.
answers.evidence: Chairman: ‘add up to three Debt freely, each +£5 Balance’; ‘Each additional advance requires consent’ of majority share controllers; ‘never pass Debt track end’; ‘allocate all Balance to other offices’ treasuries.’

answers.answer: Shipping must spend its treasury until £2 or less remains. It may lease an extra ship for £2, fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 without the owner's consent, or buy a Company ship for £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Put each acquired ship in any sea zone, including China if its office exists. Extra ships are temporary and return to supply at Refresh.
answers.evidence: Manager of Shipping: ‘spend treasury until £2 or less remains’; lease £2, fit £3 ‘without owner consent,’ buy Company ship £5 ‘only if no ships remain on shipyards’; extra ships last until Refresh.

answers.answer: The President declares the home region and any other regions reachable through open orders with available ship capacity. Each £1 from the President's treasury buys one die; subtract one die per declared nonhome region. Failure may be retried during that President's uninterrupted opportunity if affordable; catastrophe removes the President, and a President can have at most one successful Trade per turn. On success, fill one order per ship in that sea zone, as many as possible within the declared regions: first place a writer at home, then each next order must be adjacent to one already filled by this Presidency. Use available writers, then filled-order tokens. A Presidency cannot fill another Presidency's home region, even if that office is vacant. Add each order's printed revenue to Balance, or half rounded down if a firm filled it this turn; the President earns £1 per order from the bank and owners earn £1 per writer placed.
answers.evidence: Presidency Trade: declare home plus reachable regions; ‘Each £1 President's treasury buys one die; subtract one per declared nonhome region’; one successful Trade limit; capacity is ‘one order per ship’; other home regions are protected; order revenue, bank and writer bonuses specified.

answers.answer: A Commander may target their Presidency's home, any associated region, or a region bordering an associated region, but not another home region or another Presidency's Company-controlled region. A Company region must have unrest or a closed order for the action to have an effect. Exhaust officers or regiments for one die each and local alliances for their printed dice; subtract the combined strength of the target and every other region in its empire, counting the target once (Company defense strength is zero). After each attempt, the owners roll one die per officer exhausted in that attempt; each 6 returns that officer to supply. Regiments do not roll officer-loss dice.
answers.evidence: Commanders and Deploy: target boundaries and Company-region condition; exhaust pieces for dice and subtract target plus empire strength; ‘After each attempt’ roll per exhausted officer, each 6 removes it; regiments never roll officer losses.

answers.answer: On successful Deploy, loot is £4 per target tower plus the faceup loot token modifier, with at least one pound per surviving used officer. Distribute it as £1 to the Commander plus £1 per surviving used officer of that Commander, £1 per other player's used surviving officer, and £1 to the bank per regiment and per alliance piece. The Commander gains one trophy per target tower. Then remove the target's tower/dome, remove all matching empire flags if it was a capital, open its orders and clear unrest; for a newly Company-controlled region, place its loot/control token region-side above the President and place the Governor overlay (the office card goes to Vacant Offices). On catastrophe, the Commander returns half their family's trophies rounded up and the Commander member returns to supply; exhausted officers still check losses, and the Commander has no office card to vacate.
answers.evidence: Deploy: ‘loot = £4 per target tower + faceup loot token's modifier’; payout cycle and ‘one trophy per target tower’; control procedure follows; catastrophe returns half trophies rounded up and Commander to supply.

answers.answer: A Governor takes the printed dice pool and may make repeated attempts; each attempt rolls the current pool without penalty, then reduces the pool by one. A success pays £1 plus another £1 if a previous roll was unsuccessful, and allows one choice: begin/build a Company ship through two successes, commission a regiment, or Tax by adding an unsplit £2 to Balance or the President's treasury. Every Tax after the first that turn adds unrest in the region. Each unsuccessful check adds unrest. The Governor can continue until choosing to stop, running out of dice, or suffering catastrophe, which removes the officeholder under the normal office rule.
answers.evidence: Governors: ‘Each attempt rolls current pool with no penalty; reduce pool one after every result’; success pays £1 plus £1 after a prior failure; tax and repeated-tax unrest; failure adds unrest; may stop, run out, or catastrophically fail.

answers.answer: Company expenses are paid first: £1 per existing Debt, each officer/regiment in an Army, and each ship in sea zones (including China), excluding Commanders. If Balance is insufficient, take £5 emergency loans and advance Debt one per loan; continue taking loans even when Debt is at the track maximum. New emergency Debt adds no expense this turn. After the loans, set Balance to zero. One or two loans reduce Standing one; three or more reduce it two. Next compare remaining Balance with expectations at current Standing; if below, lower Standing one. Then the Chairman may pay any affordable number of dividends, each costing one per Company share and paying each owner £1 per share, including the Chairman. If total dividend cash paid is strictly greater than expectations, raise Standing one.
answers.evidence: Revenue: emergency loans ‘even at maximum Debt’; new Debt has no current expense; set Balance to zero; loan-count Standing losses, then current-Standing expectations, then dividends and strict-greater-than expectations test.

answers.answer: An Invasion or Rebellion against a Company region also triggers secondary Rebellions in every other Company region with unrest. Resolve the primary attack first, then secondary attacks in Bombay, Madras, Bengal order, with each Commander ordering attacks in their Presidency. A normal primary Crisis uses its normal Invasion/Rebellion strength plus unrest in the target; a primary Foreign Invasion uses only its ordinary attack die, with no unrest added. Each secondary Rebellion's strength is only the number of unrest cubes in that secondary region, without an event modifier or empire strength. The associated Commander exhausts active Army pieces totaling that strength, or as much as possible; alliances use printed strength and cannot be split. Insufficient newly exhausted defense strength causes Region Loss. Sufficient defense removes all unrest and gives the Commander a trophy; if it defeats a normal primary Invasion, it also removes one tower from the attacker if possible. If the Commander is vacant, Military Affairs acts, or the Chairman if Military Affairs is vacant; that substitute chooses pieces but gains/loses no trophies. A successful primary Invasion against the Company also applies empire growth.
answers.evidence: Attacks on Company: secondary attacks occur in all other unrest Company regions, primary then ‘Bombay, Madras, Bengal’; primary/secondary strengths differ; sufficient defense removes unrest and grants trophy, insufficient defense causes Region Loss.

answers.answer: A vote at support −1 or less fails: discard the law, resolve a dilemma's If Failed text, transfer the PM dial to the Opposition Leader, and have the new PM move the proposed policy one space in either direction and resolve that adjacent policy. At support zero or higher, the law passes: place it among passed laws, the PM takes a passed-law token, resolve the selected policy first, then the law's immediate effects. Finally restore all cards used for voting to their regular orientation after either outcome. If a law causes Company failure, finish the vote before final scoring.
answers.evidence: Parliament Resolution: ‘-1 or less fails’; PM dial and policy movement; ‘Zero or higher passes’; resolve selected policy ‘then immediate law effects’; restore voting cards finally.

answers.answer: In 1758 and Long 1710, at the start of a turn before London Season, the PM may call the special Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is on a starred space. If it passes, reduce Debt by one per two current Debt, set Standing to S, give the PM a passed-law token, and activate firms. If it fails, increase Company share scoring value by flipping/placing the Court VP token, up to its ±3 maximum. This vote has no policy; failure does not remove the PM or discard the Deregulation law, and the PM may vote against it. 1813 starts deregulated.
answers.evidence: Deregulation: in 1758/Long 1710 PM may vote on lined spaces and ‘must’ on starred spaces; pass and fail effects listed; ‘No policy accompanies this law’; 1813 begins deregulated.

answers.answer: To form a firm, a player must currently manage none. They return one eligible Company share to supply or flip a workshop to its invested side; that creates the first firm share, sets value to the leftmost track space, and takes £5 from the bank into the London treasury. To invest in a firm, the manager must consent; the same share/workshop contribution creates a firm share and £5 from the bank. A firm is capped at ten shares, but further investments still contribute £5 without creating shares. The Chairman's share cannot be invested, Company shares cannot be used when Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and shares created this turn cannot be invested even if traded away. Invested workshops never become uninvested, earn no workshop bonus or Company-failure VP, and remain invested if the firm fails.
answers.evidence: Firms phase: form only if managing none; contribute Company share/workshop and take ‘£5 bank to London treasury’; investment consent, lined-space and current-turn share restrictions; ten-share cap; invested workshop consequences.

answers.answer: Each manager secretly selects a sea zone/home port and London cash bid, and needs at least one ship; alternatively they may select Hobnob with no bid, no trade and no dividends, while still paying expenses and retaining the previous dividend marker. Bids are revealed simultaneously but strategies stay facedown until the associated Presidency begins. Before that Presidency takes actions, each matching firm reveals its strategy, rolls one die per bid pound, and pays the bid to the bank; at least one 1 or 2 enables trade. Firm initiative equals ship count minus successful bid dice and may be negative. A successful President's Trade produces initiative the same way; lowest initiative fills first. The President chooses ties among traders; if the President is vacant or never successfully trades, firms fill after Commander/Governor opportunities and the Chairman chooses ties. A firm gets one trade attempt per turn and fills up to ships + 1 open orders, starting at its home port and tracing its own filled route; it may fill each particular order only once, but can refill an order another trader filled this turn. Previously filled orders pay half listed revenue, rounded down. Advance firm Value one space for each full £6 added to its India treasury that turn.
answers.evidence: Firm strategies and competing trade: secret zone/bid, reveal timing, die checks and initiative; order of tied traders; capacity ‘up to ships + 1’; previously filled order pays half; Value advances per full £6.

answers.answer: At the start of Revenue, a firm pays £1 per charter ship plus the higher of its share count or Value, using either or both firm treasuries. Dividends are paid only from India: each dividend pays £1 per firm share plus £1 to the manager. With the manager's consent, a shareholder can forgo payment for any number of their shares. Record total actual cash paid out on the dividend marker; an active non-Hobnob firm that pays nothing records zero, while Hobnob keeps its previous marker. Sweep remaining India cash into London. If the firm cannot pay expenses, it dissolves unless rescued: emergency investments follow normal share/workshop rules (even if the ten-share limit blocks new shares), pay expenses, lose remaining cash, and lower Value one per investment; alternatively it may merge with one other firm, which must first pay its own expenses if not already paid and cover the unpaid amount. On dissolution, shares go to Debtor's Prison for −1 VP each, ships return to shipyards, the charter returns to the family side, and workshops remain invested.
answers.evidence: Firm expenses, rescue and dividends: expense formula and eligible treasuries; India-only dividend calculation and marker; inability to pay leads to dissolution unless rescued; dissolution destinations and Prison penalty.
